Marie (Revenue Ops): @channel quick update on billing behaviour we9re rolling out next month — please read if you own any customer-facing quota or rate-limit docs.

Marie (Revenue Ops): TL;DR: starting 2026-04-20 we9re introducing 'consumption smoothing' (a short rolling buffer that prevents immediate hard overage charges for brief spikes) + a new tiered free-credit model that better aligns credits with account activity. Invoices will include a new line item called "smoothing adjustment" for transparency.

Dan (Billing): Details: 1) Consumption smoothing window = 72 hours rolling. Traffic that exceeds soft quotas inside that window is not immediately billed as an overage charge; we record it and apply a single reconciliation entry on the next invoice. 2) Free credits move from a flat monthly slab to an adaptive, tiered pool based on account age and usage percentiles. 3) No retroactive charges for usage that falls back under quota within the smoothing window.

Marie (Revenue Ops): Why we9re doing this: reduce customer-impact from short bursts (e.g., CI jobs, analytics jobs misfires) while keeping long-term fairness and predictability for revenue.

Sam (Engineering): Heads up for engineers: we added a flag in usage events `smoothing_applied: true|false`. Exported via webhook/usage API so your billing dashboards can show both raw tokens and billed tokens. Example curl to fetch reconciliation summary: 

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/:acct_id/usage?reconcile=true"
```

Dan (Billing): Example for transparency (simple): if a customer has a 1M token monthly quota and bursts 200k tokens for two days but averages back under quota by day 3, the burst is recorded and then the smoothing adjustment will be $0 on invoice. If the cumulative month-end usage is above quota, we charge only the net over-quota tokens after smoothing.

Ashley (Support): Support plan: we9re shipping customer-facing copy + FAQ templates tomorrow. If a customer asks for an exception for a one-time large import, escalate with the tag `billing-exception` and include the `smoothing-window` timestamps. Support will have a pre-approved playbook for 1x exception credits.

billing-bot: NOTE: Billing UI will show a temporary banner for 30 days explaining smoothing and how to read the reconciliation line item.

Sam (Engineering): SDK changes: `redwood.usage.report()` now accepts `meta.smoothing_hint` (optional). No action required for older SDKs — they9ll still report raw usage; reconciliation logic happens server-side.

Dan (Billing): Timeline & rollout: alpha internal -> next two weeks; beta customers + opt-in -> 2026-04-06; full opt-outless rollout -> 2026-04-20. We9ll publish migration notes and a CSV showing pre/post examples for accounts that moved to the adaptive free credits.

Marie (Revenue Ops): Billing visibility: the new invoice CSV will include columns: `raw_tokens`,`smoothing_buffer_adjustment`,`billed_tokens`,`free_credit_adjustment`. Export format stays compatible but we added the new columns.

Ashley (Support): Customer comms: we will email customers with >10k monthly tokens and also surface a banner in console for free-tier accounts. Templates are in #docs and will be linked in the rollout PR.

Dan (Billing): Quick policy note: this does not change SLA credits or contractual overage terms for Dedicated customers on reserved capacity. Those contracts are handled case-by-case.

Marie (Revenue Ops): Compliance note: smoothing adjustments are audited and logged; finance will keep a reconciliation ledger for GAAP. If you need the audit export, DM Dan.

Sam (Engineering): Monitoring: new metric `billing.smoothing.reconciliations.count` appears in Console; alert if reconciliations spike > 3x baseline — that likely indicates a change in traffic pattern or a misconfigured client.

Dan (Billing): If you have automated tooling that expects invoices to always match raw token count, update to use `billed_tokens` column instead. We9ll keep `raw_tokens` for debugging.

Marie (Revenue Ops): Links: policy doc (internal) -> /docs/internal/billing/consumption-smoothing.md ; rollout checklist PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/514 ; example invoice CSV -> https://s3.redwood.company/samples/smoothing-example.csv

Ashley (Support): We9re preparing outbound copy now. If you have a large customer who should get a personalized heads-up, post a note here with customer name and POC and we9ll coordinate.

Dan (Billing): FAQ highlights we expect in first 48h: "Will I be charged more?" -> usually no; smoothing reduces surprise. "Can I opt out?" -> beta opt-ins only before 2026-04-20; enterprise/legal deals may require carve-outs.

Marie (Revenue Ops): Thanks all. Please read the internal doc and leave any concerns before EOD Friday — we want to lock the email copy. :sparkles:

Ashley (Support): adding the support templates to #docs now.

Dan (Billing): filing the PR to add `smoothing_applied` to the export schema.

Marie (Revenue Ops): Ping me or Dan for anything urgent.
